plan_a_advantages: Reduced risk of overtraining due to the high volume of easy runs.
Potentially better for athletes prioritizing recovery and minimizing fatigue.
plan_b_advantages: Directly addresses speed development with a tempo run.
Incorporates cross-training for a more well-rounded fitness profile.
Includes longer runs to build trail-specific endurance.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a tempo run to build threshold strength, a crucial component for sustained speed on trails, alongside longer runs to improve endurance. Plan A, conversely, focuses almost exclusively on very easy runs, which, while beneficial for recovery, won't directly translate to increased speed. The inclusion of cross-training in Plan B also provides a valuable low-impact workout to supplement the running, preventing overuse injuries and promoting overall fitness. Plan A’s repetitive easy runs risk becoming monotonous and failing to challenge the athlete sufficiently for performance gains.
